doorway: I keep needing to pee at night, and my bladder feels uncomfortable as it fills.
Vital signs are available on the chart.
Perform a focused history and physical examination, discuss your plan, and document only what you obtain.

plan.notice: Frequency, urgency, nocturia and large urine volumes are distinct symptoms; separate them before choosing a cause.
plan.anchor: Frequency versus volume, pain versus urgency
plan.pivot: Ask voiding pattern, relation of discomfort to filling and emptying, fluid and caffeine intake, thirst and glycemic symptoms.
plan.exam: Assess the abdomen and relevant general findings. Use proposed urine and metabolic testing to evaluate alternatives rather than declaring them excluded.
plan.avoid: Calling frequency polyuria without a volume history or overlooking caffeine and other irritants.

goals: Distinguish frequent small voids from polyuria and incomplete emptying.
Connect discomfort with bladder filling and relief after voiding.
Exclude infection and reproductive causes before assigning a chronic bladder diagnosis.
